argument_summary: The certification case should be read narrowly. The admissible record supports release readiness at the aggregate level and supports reversible, monitored deployment, but it also preserves an unresolved limitation for the cybersecurity alert triage use case. The defensible position is not that rollout controls cured the weakness. It is that certification can proceed only on a disclosed, caveated basis where the model card expressly states the exposed limitation, the record does not treat the draft risk acceptance as approved coverage, and monitoring plus rollback are additional governance controls rather than substitutes for the policy predicate.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the argument. The narrower point is that escalation is unnecessary if the auditor treats this as a disclosed residual-risk release with bounded monitoring and rollback, rather than as a claim that the weakness was resolved. That approach preserves audit accuracy without overstating what the evidence proves.
claims_about_policy: The policy evidence cuts against any claim of clean compliance based on rollout controls alone. The applicable rule says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless they are resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and the policy text provided in context says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or include reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. On this record, neither exclusion nor approved risk acceptance is established. The supportable reading is therefore limited: disclosure remains mandatory, the unresolved exposure must stay explicit in the certification record, and the release can be defended only as caveated compliance rather than as policy satisfaction by controls alone.
concessions: The current record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls alone satisfy the internal policy predicate.
The cybersecurity alert triage segment remains below target on lateral-movement alert summarization and remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
The risk-acceptance draft is not approved on its face and does not expressly cover the exposed cybersecurity alert triage segment.
Public model-card and monitoring guidance supports governance process, but it does not by itself prove that the internal certification standard is fully met for the exposed use case.
